logic.note: Espressif AT firmware 1.7 behaviour for what sketches use: AT, ATE0/1, AT+RST (boot ROM text at 74880 baud, then ready), GMR, UART_DEF/UART_CUR/CIOBAUD, CWMODE, CWLAP, CWJAP (+CWJAP:<code> FAIL), CWQAP, CIFSR, CIPMUX 0/1, CIPSTART TCP/SSL (DNS Fail, ALREADY CONNECTED, no ip), CIPSEND with the > prompt, Recv n bytes / SEND OK, +IPD delivery, CLOSED, CIPCLOSE, CIPSTATUS, CIPDOMAIN, PING, busy p..., auto-reconnect after a Wi-Fi loss. Transparent mode (CIPMODE=1), server mode and AT+HTTPCLIENT are not emulated.

timing.note: Bit-exact UART at the module's baud rate, both directions, on the board's pins. Command delays are typical figures (join 1.5 s + 0.9 s for the IP on an open network, 3.6 s to report a wrong password, 25 ms DNS, TCP connect from the sandbox host, SSL adds its handshake time); a real module varies by hundreds of ms with the AP and the radio.

analog.note: TX drives 3.3 V through 40 Ω; RX, EN and RST have the ESP-01S 12 kΩ pull-ups. 5 V on RX is reported, not simulated as damage.

power.note: A constant 80 mA load on VCC. Real transmit peaks of 170 to 300 mA (which brown out an Uno's 3V3 pin and reset the module) are not modelled.

radio.note: No RF: the sandbox network decides joins, DNS and TCP. Signal strength is fixed at -52 dBm, there is no packet loss, retransmission or TLS certificate check, and a Wi-Fi drop is an injected fault (set esp.wifi = down) or a network-wide fault.

emulates: The AT command set a sketch uses to join Wi-Fi and make HTTP requests over TCP or SSL
Echo, busy and error replies, +IPD framing with and without CIPMUX
Baud rate changes (factory 115200, AT+UART_DEF=9600 for SoftwareSerial)
Boot output at 74880 baud that sketches must ignore
Wi-Fi loss with WIFI DISCONNECT, CLOSED links and automatic reconnection
Wrong SSID / password failures with their +CWJAP codes
EN and RST pins, power below 3.0 V and above 3.6 V
doesNotEmulate: Radio range, interference, packet loss and real Wi-Fi association
TLS handshake CPU cost and certificate validation
Current peaks that brown out a weak 3.3 V supply
Transparent (passthrough) mode, AT+CIPSERVER, AT+HTTPCLIENT, SmartConfig, WPS
The 115200-baud receive errors SoftwareSerial makes on a real Uno
testOnRealDevice: Power the ESP-01 from a 3.3 V regulator that gives 300 mA (AMS1117-3.3 with 10 µF + 100 nF), not the Uno 3V3 pin: random resets and 'busy p...' are the symptom
Put a 1 kΩ / 2 kΩ divider on the module's RX
Set the module to 9600 baud once (AT+UART_DEF=9600,8,1,0,0) before using SoftwareSerial
Your Wi-Fi name and password in the sketch, and the gateway's LAN address (http://<your-computer>:8787) instead of ai.jumper
Check the AT firmware version with AT+GMR: 1.7.x matches the sandbox; very old 0.9.x firmware answers differently
